BiblicalUsage: This word means to blind, and it works two ways in Scripture. A gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, so Moses forbids judges to take one. And in judgment, Zedekiah's eyes were put out at Riblah after watching his sons killed — blinded in fact because he had been blind in heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that bribes blind because they make us see what we are paid to see. Zedekiah's story is the end of that road, and I want my eyes kept clear by refusing the gift.
